journey.title: Open and close the Sort drawer, then apply a filter from the drawer with an autofocus field, all with the keyboard
journey.goal: Opening the drawer moves focus into it, so the user can tick a filter and show results without a pointer

functionalJourney.title: Apply a filter with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking Filters, ticking Waterproof and clicking Show results applies the filter

guards.title: Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to Filters
guards.goal: After opening the drawer with the pointer, Escape closes it and focus is back on the Filters button

plan.root_cause: The Drawer component does not manage focus when opening a dialog. After showModal()/show() is called, focus remains on the triggering element or body, leaving keyboard users disoriented. The expected behavior is to move focus to the first focusable element inside the drawer (or an element with autofocus).
plan.repair_strategy: Add a private _enforceFocus method to DialogBase that focuses the autofocus element if present, otherwise the first focusable element. Call this method at the end of _showElement after showing the dialog.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: When opening the Sort or Filters drawer via keyboard (Enter on the toggle button), focus will move into the drawer to the first focusable element (or autofocus element). This allows users to interact with filter controls without needing a mouse, fulfilling WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.4.3 Focus Order.
functional_risks: Adding focus logic could interfere with custom focus management if a subclass already handles focus (though none currently do).
The focusable selector may not match all possible focusable edge cases (e.g., web components with tabindex). However, it covers standard HTML controls.
Calling focus() may cause scroll adjustments if the target is not visible; but the drawer is shown at viewport start, so impact is minimal.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Enter on #sort-open opens the sort drawer and focuses #sort-close.
Verify that pressing Enter on #filters-open opens the filters drawer and focuses #filters-search (due to autofocus).
Verify that Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to the toggle button.
Verify that Tab traversal works correctly within each drawer.
Verify that the drawer can still be opened via mouse/touch and that focus behavior remains appropriate.

plan.root_cause: The Drawer component's _getShowOptions returns modal: true for side drawers (due to backdrop: true default), causing showModal() to be used instead of show(). This centers the dialog natively, conflicts with side-drawer CSS positioning, and fails to trap focus in the side-positioned drawer, leaving focus on body.
plan.repair_strategy: Change Drawer._getShowOptions to always return modal: false for side drawers, so show() is used and _enforceFocus (in DialogBase._showElement) explicitly focuses the first focusable element (autofocus or close button).
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can open Sort and Filters drawers and immediately interact with controls (close button, search input, checkboxes) because focus moves into the drawer on open.
functional_risks: If any Drawer variant requires modal behavior (centered, focus-trapped), it will lose that; but Drawer is documented for side drawers only.
Backdrop click handling remains unchanged (handled in DialogBase).
verification_requirements: Press Enter on #sort-open → Sort drawer opens, focus lands on #sort-close.
Press Escape → Sort drawer closes, focus returns to #sort-open.
Press Enter on #filters-open → Filters drawer opens, focus lands on #filters-search (autofocus).
Tab through Filters drawer controls (search, checkboxes, apply button) works.
Form submission updates #applied text and closes Filters drawer.

plan.root_cause: The DialogBase class does not enforce focus when a drawer/dialog is shown, leaving focus on the triggering element or body. Additionally, it does not store the relatedTarget to restore focus when the drawer is closed via Escape, relying solely on the data API's hidden event listener which may fire too late or not at all in automated tests.
plan.repair_strategy: 1. Import isVisible utility. 2. Add _relatedTarget property to track the triggering element. 3. In _show, store relatedTarget. 4. In _showElement, call _enforceFocus() after showing the dialog to move focus to the first focusable/autofocus element. 5. In _closeAndCleanup, restore focus to _relatedTarget if visible, then clear it.
